independence: Reviewer did not author this PCM batch.
referencePolicy: Korean target text and course/question context take precedence over shortened English gloss; English reference is not evidence of omitted person gender.

records.source: 밥을 먹어요. (babeul meogeoyo.) = I eat a meal.
records.translation: 밥을 먹어요. (babeul meogeoyo.) = I dey chop food.
records.reason: Food-eating statement becomes I dey chop food; object and first-person reference match the English gloss without gender assignment.

records.source: 밥 (rice, a meal), 빵 (bread), 과일 (fruit), 고기 (meat), 물 (water), 우유 (milk).
records.translation: 밥 (rice or food), 빵 (bread), 과일 (fruit), 고기 (meat), 물 (water), 우유 (milk).
records.reason: Rice/meal, bread, fruit, meat, water and milk meanings remain associated with the correct Korean nouns; shared loan nouns are not automatically English fallback.
Bread and fruit are common shared food nouns; both Korean labels and their romanizations stay correctly paired.

records.source: Say what you like with -를/을 좋아해요 and what you don't like with -를/을 싫어해요: 저는 사과를 좋아해요.
records.translation: Use -를/을 좋아해요 to talk wetin you like and -를/을 싫어해요 for wetin you no like: 저는 사과를 좋아해요.
records.reason: Like versus dislike and both Korean object-particle alternatives remain distinct.
I like am preserves liking the unspecified object; am does not assign human gender.

records.source: Describing words also end in -요: 커요 (big), 작아요 (small), 많아요 (many), 맛있어요 (delicious), 예뻐요 (pretty).
records.translation: Describing words dey end with -요 too: 커요 (big), 작아요 (small), 많아요 (plenty), 맛있어요 (sweet to chop), 예뻐요 (fine).
records.reason: Big/small/many/tasty/pretty meanings remain mapped correctly; sweet to chop means palatable here, not a new sugar claim.

records.source: 커요. (keoyo.) = It's big. / 작아요. (jagayo.) = It's small.
records.translation: 커요. (keoyo.) = E big. / 작아요. (jagayo.) = E small.
records.reason: E big/E small preserves size contrast without inferring a person’s gender.

records.source: 날씨 (weather), 더워요 (it's hot), 추워요 (it's cold), 비가 와요 (it's raining), 눈이 와요 (it's snowing).
records.translation: 날씨 (weather), 더워요 (e hot), 추워요 (e cold), 비가 와요 (rain dey fall), 눈이 와요 (snow dey fall).
records.reason: Heat/cold/rain/snow and weather meanings remain distinct.

records.source: 더워요. (deowoyo.) = It's hot. / 추워요. (chuwoyo.) = It's cold.
records.translation: 더워요. (deowoyo.) = E hot. / 추워요. (chuwoyo.) = E cold.
records.reason: Hot/cold contrast preserved with neutral e.

records.source: Put **안** before a verb to say you don't do something (안 가요). Put **못** before it to say you can't (못 가요).
records.translation: Put **안** before verb to talk say you no do something (안 가요). Put **못** before am to talk say you no fit do am (못 가요).
records.reason: 안 negation and 못 inability are distinguished by no do versus no fit do.

records.source: 안 먹어요. (an meogeoyo.) = I don't eat.
records.translation: 안 먹어요. (an meogeoyo.) = I no dey chop.
records.reason: No dey chop preserves negative eating; no capability claim added.

records.source: 일어나요 (wake up), 씻어요 (wash), 일해요 (work), 자요 (sleep). Time words such as 아침 (morning) and 밤 (night) take 에: 아침에.
records.translation: 일어나요 (wake up), 씻어요 (wash), 일해요 (work), 자요 (sleep). Time words like 아침 (morning) and 밤 (night) dey take 에: 아침에.
records.reason: Wake/wash/work/sleep and morning/night temporal 에 remain properly associated.
Wake-up meaning remains correct.
Yesterday/today/tomorrow shared calendar vocabulary retains all three times.

records.source: Time words usually come near the start of the sentence.
records.translation: Time words normally dey near di start of sentence.
records.reason: Sentence-initial tendency of time words is kept as normally, not an absolute rule.
Korean time words and corresponding romanizations are the actual learning target; unchanged correctly.
Wetin I don do is an appropriate completed-action heading.

records.source: Past tense: **-았어요 / -었어요 / -했어요**. Some verbs shorten: 가다 → 갔어요, 보다 → 봤어요.
records.translation: Past tense: **-았어요 / -었어요 / -했어요**. Some verbs dey shorten: 가다 → 갔어요, 보다 → 봤어요.
records.reason: Past endings and both contraction examples are preserved; source’s simplified grammar rule is not independently certified.
I don chop conveys completed eating; no gender assumption.
Wetin I go do retains future-action heading.

records.source: Use **-(으)ㄹ 거예요** for plans: 가다 → 갈 거예요, 먹다 → 먹을 거예요.
records.translation: Use **-(으)ㄹ 거예요** for plans: 가다 → 갈 거예요, 먹다 → 먹을 거예요.
records.reason: The plan instruction and -(으)ㄹ 거예요 examples retain meaning, but an entire imperative sentence is labeled shared_technical_term; role clarity needs adjustment.

suggestedPatch.guidance: Full learner instruction is not a technical term. Retain the same Korean/romanization content; native Naijá wording should be checked rather than certified by English overlap.

records.source: 내일 갈 거예요. (naeil gal geoyeyo.) = I will go tomorrow.
records.translation: 내일 갈 거예요. (naeil gal geoyeyo.) = I go go tomorrow.
records.reason: I go go tomorrow retains going in the future and tomorrow.

records.source: 월요일 (Mon), 화요일 (Tue), 수요일 (Wed), 목요일 (Thu), 금요일 (Fri), 토요일 (Sat), 일요일 (Sun).
records.translation: 월요일 (Mon), 화요일 (Tue), 수요일 (Wed), 목요일 (Thu), 금요일 (Fri), 토요일 (Sat), 일요일 (Sun).
records.reason: Seven Korean weekdays retain their corresponding standard calendar abbreviations; names are shared calendar labels.
Korean weekdays and romanizations are protected learning targets.

records.source: Months are a Sino-Korean number plus 월: 일월 (January), 삼월 (March), 오월 (May), 칠월 (July), 구월 (September), 십이월 (December).
records.translation: For months, use Sino-Korean number plus 월: 일월 (January), 삼월 (March), 오월 (May), 칠월 (July), 구월 (September), 십이월 (December).
records.reason: Sino-Korean month construction and all six named months remain aligned.
Korean month targets and their romanizations remain unchanged.

records.source: Hours use native numbers plus 시: 한 시 (1:00), 두 시 (2:00), 세 시 (3:00), 열 시 (10:00). Ask 몇 시예요?
records.translation: For hours, use native numbers plus 시: 한 시 (1:00), 두 시 (2:00), 세 시 (3:00), 열 시 (10:00). Ask 몇 시예요?
records.reason: Native-number hours plus 시, four times, and question 몇 시예요? are preserved.

records.source: 한 시 · 두 시 · 세 시 (han si · du si · se si)
records.translation: 한 시 · 두 시 · 세 시 (han si · du si · se si)
records.reason: Korean hour examples and romanizations are protected targets.

records.source: 매일 (every day), 자주 (often), 가끔 (sometimes), 항상 (always). Place them before the verb.
records.translation: 매일 (every day), 자주 (often), 가끔 (sometimes), 항상 (always). Put them before di verb.
records.reason: Daily/often/sometimes/always frequency distinctions and placement before the verb are retained.
Every day/sometimes are shared everyday expressions; they convey the correct frequency meanings.

records.source: The past ending is -았/었어요: 했어요 (did), 왔어요 (came), 만났어요 (met), 샀어요 (bought), 잤어요 (slept).
records.translation: Past ending na -았/었어요: 했어요 (did), 왔어요 (came), 만났어요 (met), 샀어요 (bought), 잤어요 (slept).
records.reason: Past-ending description and did/came/met/bought/slept align with Korean forms; shared English lexical forms are understandable but Naijá aspect choices need native fluency review.
Don do expresses completed doing.

records.source: 생일 (birthday), 주말 (weekend), 선물 (gift). Ask 생일이 언제예요? and answer 제 생일은 오월이에요.
records.translation: 생일 (birthday), 주말 (weekend), 선물 (gift). Ask 생일이 언제예요? and answer 제 생일은 오월이에요.
records.reason: Birthday/weekend/gift meanings and question/answer remain correct, but the whole two-sentence instruction is not merely a technical term.

suggestedPatch.guidance: Full learner instruction is not a technical term. Retain the same Korean/romanization content; native Naijá wording should be checked rather than certified by English overlap.

records.source: 생일이 언제예요? (saengiri eonjeyeyo?) = When is your birthday?
records.translation: 생일이 언제예요? (saengiri eonjeyeyo?) = When be your birthday?
records.reason: When be your birthday retains birthday timing question.
For shop is an appropriate location heading.

records.source: Ask the price with 얼마예요? and ask for something with **… 주세요** (… please).
records.translation: Ask price with 얼마예요? and use **… 주세요** (… abeg) to ask for something.
records.reason: Price question and … 주세요 request construction retain their distinct functions; abeg corresponds to please.
How much e be preserves the price question.
Where e dey preserves the location question.

records.source: Ask **… 어디예요?** (Where is …?). Listen for 오른쪽 (right), 왼쪽 (left) and 직진 (straight).
records.translation: Ask **… 어디예요?** (Where … dey?). Listen for 오른쪽 (right), 왼쪽 (left) and 직진 (straight).
records.reason: Location question, right/left/straight directions remain correctly paired.

records.source: 화장실이 어디예요? (hwajangsiri eodiyeyo?) = Where is the restroom?
records.translation: 화장실이 어디예요? (hwajangsiri eodiyeyo?) = Where toilet dey?
records.reason: Where toilet dey preserves restroom-location question.
I wan retains desire rather than future certainty.

records.source: Add **-고 싶어요** to a verb stem to say what you want to do: 가다 → 가고 싶어요.
records.translation: Add **-고 싶어요** to verb stem to talk wetin you wan do: 가다 → 가고 싶어요.
records.reason: Want-to ending and 가다→가고 싶어요 derivation preserved.

records.source: 가고 싶어요. (gago sipeoyo.) = I want to go.
records.translation: 가고 싶어요. (gago sipeoyo.) = I wan go.
records.reason: I wan go preserves desire to go.

records.source: 메뉴 (menu), 주문할게요 (I'll order), 물 더 주세요 (more water, please), 계산해 주세요 (the bill, please).
records.translation: 메뉴 (menu), 주문할게요 (I go order), 물 더 주세요 (more water, abeg), 계산해 주세요 (bring di bill, abeg).
records.reason: Menu, ordering commitment, extra water request and bill request remain distinct.

records.source: 계산해 주세요. (gyesanhae juseyo.) = The bill, please.
records.translation: 계산해 주세요. (gyesanhae juseyo.) = Di bill, abeg.
records.reason: Di bill, abeg preserves the polite bill request.

records.source: 버스 (bus), 지하철 (subway), 택시 (taxi), 기차 (train). Say how you go with -로/으로: 버스로 가요.
records.translation: 버스 (bus), 지하철 (underground train), 택시 (taxi), 기차 (train). Use -로/으로 to talk how you dey go: 버스로 가요.
records.reason: Bus/subway/taxi/train and transport particle -로/으로 remain aligned; underground train is an accurate subway gloss.
Bus and underground train remain correct transport meanings.

records.source: 전화 (phone call), 전화번호 (phone number), 문자 (text message). 전화해요 means “I call”.
records.translation: 전화 (phone call), 전화번호 (phone number), 문자 (text message). 전화해요 mean “I dey call”.
records.reason: Call, phone number and text-message nouns stay distinct; I dey call is a viable present-action gloss.
Phone call is a common shared noun phrase; Korean noun and romanization are retained.

records.source: 병원 (hospital), 약 (medicine), 아파요 (it hurts). Say the body part first: 머리가 아파요 (my head hurts).
records.translation: 병원 (hospital), 약 (medicine), 아파요 (e dey pain). Talk di body part first: 머리가 아파요 (my head dey pain).
records.reason: Hospital/medicine/pain and body-part-first headache example remain correct.

records.translation: 병원 (byeongwon) = hospital / 아파요. (apayo.) = E dey pain.
records.reason: Hospital and pain statement remain distinct.

records.source: -세요 and -아/어 주세요 make polite requests: 앉으세요 (please sit), 기다려 주세요 (please wait), 문을 열어 주세요 (please open the door).
records.translation: -세요 and -아/어 주세요 dey make polite requests: 앉으세요 (abeg sit), 기다려 주세요 (abeg wait), 문을 열어 주세요 (abeg open di door).
records.reason: Sit/wait/open-door polite requests and both Korean request forms remain correctly paired.
Abeg wait preserves the polite waiting request.

records.source: 같이 (together) invites someone: 같이 가요. 갈래요? asks “Do you want to go?” and 시간 있어요? asks “Do you have time?”
records.translation: Use 같이 (together) to invite person: 같이 가요. 갈래요? dey ask “You wan go?” and 시간 있어요? dey ask “You get time?”
records.reason: Together invitation, desire-to-go question and time-availability question are distinct.

records.source: 같이 가요. (gachi gayo.) = Let's go together.
records.translation: 같이 가요. (gachi gayo.) = Make we go together.
records.reason: Make we go together retains inclusive suggestion, not a command to another person alone.
Formal polite endings is an accurate grammar heading; native Naijá classroom terminology remains outside this review’s certification.

records.source: In formal speech and at work, attach -ㅂ니다 to a verb or adjective stem that ends in a vowel and -습니다 to a stem that ends in a consonant. Questions end in -ㅂ니까 / -습니까.
records.translation: For formal speech and work, add -ㅂ니다 to verb or adjective stem wey end with vowel, and -습니다 to stem wey end with consonant. Questions dey end with -ㅂ니까 / -습니까.
records.reason: Vowel/consonant distinctions and formal statement/question endings are preserved; source simplification is not a comprehensive grammar approval.

records.source: 저는 학생입니다. (jeoneun haksaengimnida.) = I am a student. / 이름이 무엇입니까? (ireumi mueosimnikka?) = What is your name?
records.translation: 저는 학생입니다. (jeoneun haksaengimnida.) = I be student. / 이름이 무엇입니까? (ireumi mueosimnikka?) = Wetin be your name?
records.reason: Student identity and name question retain first-person versus addressee distinction and no gender assumption.
Plain forms accurately names the grammar category, but native pedagogical terminology needs review.

records.source: The plain (written) style ends statements in -ㄴ다 / -는다 and past statements in -았다 / -었다. These forms are the base for reported speech in the next lessons.
records.translation: Plain written style dey end statements with -ㄴ다 / -는다 and past statements with -았다 / -었다. These forms na di base for reported speech for di next lessons.
records.reason: Plain written statements and past endings preserve the reported-speech relationship; source’s coverage is simplified.

records.source: 나는 학교에 간다. (naneun hakgyoe ganda.) = I go to school. / 동생은 책을 읽는다. (dongsaengeun chaegeul ingneunda.) = My younger sibling reads a book.
records.translation: 나는 학교에 간다. (naneun hakgyoe ganda.) = I dey go school. / 동생은 책을 읽는다. (dongsaengeun chaegeul ingneunda.) = My younger sibling dey read book.
records.reason: Younger sibling stays gender-unspecified. Sibling is an English-derived abstract kinship term; native Naijá fluency cannot be certified here.
Describe nouns preserves the noun-modification heading.

records.source: A verb or adjective can describe a noun: -(으)ㄴ for adjectives and past actions, -는 for present actions, -(으)ㄹ for future or planned actions, placed before the noun.
records.translation: Verb or adjective fit describe noun: put -(으)ㄴ for adjectives and past actions, -는 for present actions, and -(으)ㄹ for future or planned actions before di noun.
records.reason: Adjectival/past versus present versus future modifiers remain distinct and placed before the noun.

records.source: 저는 맛있는 음식을 좋아해요. (jeoneun masinneun eumsigeul joahaeyo.) = I like delicious food. / 예쁜 꽃을 샀어요. (yeppeun kkocheul sasseoyo.) = I bought pretty flowers.
records.translation: 저는 맛있는 음식을 좋아해요. (jeoneun masinneun eumsigeul joahaeyo.) = I like food wey sweet. / 예쁜 꽃을 샀어요. (yeppeun kkocheul sasseoyo.) = I don buy fine flowers.
records.reason: Liking tasty food and completed purchase of pretty flowers remain correct; no person gender added.
Basic connectors is a shared grammar-category heading; this is not an independently approved Naijá terminology choice.

records.source: Join two clauses with -아/어서 (reason or sequence), -지만 (contrast), -(으)니까 (reason), -(으)면 (if) and -(으)려고 (in order to).
records.translation: Join two clauses with -아/어서 (reason or sequence), -지만 (contrast), -(으)니까 (reason), -(으)면 (if) and -(으)려고 (to show purpose).
records.reason: Reason/sequence, contrast, reason, condition and purpose stay aligned with their Korean connectors.

records.source: 피곤해서 일찍 잤어요. (pigonhaeseo iljjik jasseoyo.) = I was tired, so I went to bed early. / 비가 와서 집에 있었어요. (biga waseo jibe isseosseoyo.) = It rained, so I stayed home.
records.translation: 피곤해서 일찍 잤어요. (pigonhaeseo iljjik jasseoyo.) = I tire, so I sleep early. / 비가 와서 집에 있었어요. (biga waseo jibe isseosseoyo.) = Rain fall, so I stay house.
records.reason: Tiredness causes early sleep and rain causes staying home; causality preserved, bare verbs can carry past in context.
Ability/obligation/permission categories retain meaning, but native classroom terminology needs review rather than assuming technical English is sufficient localization.

records.source: -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 expresses ability or possibility, -아/어야 하다 obligation, and -아/어도 되다 permission.
records.translation: -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 dey express ability or possibility, -아/어야 하다 obligation, and -아/어도 되다 permission.
records.reason: Ability/possibility, obligation and permission remain separated, including 있다/없다 positive/negative capacity forms.

records.source: 저는 수영할 수 있어요. (jeoneun suyeonghal su isseoyo.) = I can swim. / 저는 한국어로 이야기할 수 있어요. (jeoneun hangugeoro iyagihal su isseoyo.) = I can talk in Korean.
records.translation: 저는 수영할 수 있어요. (jeoneun suyeonghal su isseoyo.) = I fit swim. / 저는 한국어로 이야기할 수 있어요. (jeoneun hangugeoro iyagihal su isseoyo.) = I fit talk Korean.
records.reason: Swimming and speaking Korean abilities use fit, without inferring gender.

records.source: Report what someone says or said: verb/adj + -다고 하다.
records.translation: Report wetin person dey talk or don talk: verb/adj + -다고 하다.
records.reason: Report wetin person dey talk or don talk preserves reported statements and present/past reporting alternatives.

records.source: 친구가 온다고 해요. (chinguga ondago haeyo.) = friend said coming
records.translation: 친구가 온다고 해요. (chinguga ondago haeyo.) = E say friend dey come.
records.reason: E is a neutral omitted reporter; friend is the embedded coming subject, not automatically the reporter. Correctly avoids abbreviated English friend-said ambiguity.
records.sourceIssue: English abbreviated friend said coming obscures reporter and embedded subject. Korean primary text leaves reporter unspecified; friend is the coming subject.

records.reason: Report question preserves reporting function and -냐고 묻다/하다 learning forms.

records.source: 어디 가냐고 물었어요. (eodi ganyago mureosseoyo.) = asked where going
records.translation: 어디 가냐고 물었어요. (eodi ganyago mureosseoyo.) = E ask where person dey go.
records.reason: Reporter e and unspecified person going are separate; no name, gender or number setting introduced.

records.source: Report an imperative (-라고 하다) or propositive (-자고 하다).
records.translation: Report command (-라고 하다) or suggestion (-자고 하다).
records.reason: Command versus suggestion reporting remains distinct and Korean forms retained.

records.source: 빨리 오라고 했어요. (ppalli orago haesseoyo.) = told to come fast / 같이 가자고 했어요. (gachi gajago haesseoyo.) = suggested go together
records.translation: 빨리 오라고 했어요. (ppalli orago haesseoyo.) = E tell person make e come quick / 같이 가자고 했어요. (gachi gajago haesseoyo.) = E suggest make we go together
records.reason: Tell person make e come quick preserves command content; make we go together preserves suggestion content.

records.source: Negative cause or delay (-느라고) and contrast despite circumstances (-는데도).
records.translation: Cause wey get negative result or delay (-느라고), and contrast despite di situation (-는데도).
records.reason: Negative-result/delay cause and despite-circumstances contrast are distinguished.

records.source: 공부하느라고 바빴어요. (gongbuhaneurago bapasseoyo.) = busy studying / 비가 오는데도 갔어요. (biga oneundedo gasseoyo.) = went despite rain
records.translation: 공부하느라고 바빴어요. (gongbuhaneurago bapasseoyo.) = E busy dey study / 비가 오는데도 갔어요. (biga oneundedo gasseoyo.) = E go even though rain dey fall
records.reason: Being busy studying and going despite rain retain meaning; e is gender-neutral and source subject remains omitted.

records.source: The more... the more (-을수록) and natural inevitability (-기 마련이다).
records.translation: Di more... di more (-을수록), and wetin normally go happen (-기 마련이다).
records.reason: Di more...di more captures proportional change; normally go happen conveys the natural tendency of -기 마련이다 without adding a new event.

records.source: 만날수록 좋아요. (mannalsurok joayo.) = better as we meet / 사람은 실수하기 마련이에요. (sarameun silsuhagi maryeonieyo.) = bound to make mistakes
records.translation: 만날수록 좋아요. (mannalsurok joayo.) = Di more di meetings, di better / 사람은 실수하기 마련이에요. (sarameun silsuhagi maryeonieyo.) = People bound to make mistakes
records.reason: Repeated meeting improves things; people making mistakes remains a general statement, not a named person’s trait.

records.source: Looks like (-아/어 보이다) and appears to be (-는 모양이다).
records.translation: E look like (-아/어 보이다), and e appear say (-는 모양이다).
records.reason: Appearance versus inferred situation descriptions remain distinct.

records.source: 행복해 보여요. (haengbokae boyeoyo.) = looks happy / 비가 오는 모양이에요. (biga oneun moyangieyo.) = seems raining
records.translation: 행복해 보여요. (haengbokae boyeoyo.) = E look happy / 비가 오는 모양이에요. (biga oneun moyangieyo.) = E be like rain dey fall
records.reason: Happy appearance and apparent rain retain non-certain inference and neutral e.

records.source: Pretend to do or be something: -(으)ㄴ/는 척하다.
records.translation: Pretend to do or be something: -(으)ㄴ/는 척하다.
records.reason: Meaning of pretending is correct, but an entire copied explanatory imperative is categorized as a technical term; native phrasing/role needs review.

suggestedPatch.guidance: Full learner instruction is not a technical term. Retain the same Korean/romanization content; native Naijá wording should be checked rather than certified by English overlap.

records.source: 아는 척해요. (aneun cheokaeyo.) = pretends to know
